abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) have become central to modern vision and vision-language models, yet how multiple attention heads interact within Multi-Head Self-Attention (MHSA) remains insufficiently explored. This work examines inter-head relations in ViTs, focusing on how different heads cooperate, compete, or encode overlap information during inference. By combining semantic analysis of attention behaviors with activation-based visualization, we characterize four relation types: expertise, collaboration, interference, and redundancy, and introduce simple quantitative measures to assess their influence on model behavior. Experiments on both base and large ViT models show consistent interaction patterns across different capacities. We further study how targeted ablation of specific head groups affects accuracy and robustness on several visual recognition benchmarks. The observations indicate that reducing interfering heads can alleviate sensitivity to spurious cues, while pruning redundant ones can improve computational efficiency without retraining. This study provides an interpretable perspective on how attention heads jointly contribute to the representations formed by Vision Transformers and highlights their potential impact on robustness and efficiency.

title: A Gradient Descent Algorithm on the Grassman Manifold for Matrix Completion

openAccessPdf.disclaimer: Notice: Paper or abstract available at https://arxiv.org/abs/0910.5260, which is subject to the license by the author or copyright owner provided with this content. Please go to the source to verify the license and copyright information for your use.

abstract: Missing and suspicious traffic data are inevitable due to detector and communication malfunctions, which adversely affect the transportation management system (TMS). In this paper, a tensor pattern which is an extension of matrix is introduced into modeling the traffic data for the first time, which can give full play to traffic spatial–temporal information and preserve the multi-way nature of traffic data. To estimate the missing value, a tensor decomposition based Imputation method has been developed. This approach not only inherits the advantages of imputation methods based on matrix pattern for estimating missing points, but also well mines the multi-dimensional inherent correlation of traffic data. Experiments demonstrate that the proposed method achieves a better imputation performance than the state-of-the-art imputation approach even when the missing ratio is up to 90%. Furthermore, the experimental results show that the proposed method can address the extreme case where the data of one or several days are completely missing, and additionally it can be employed to recover the missing traffic data in adverse weather as well.
